title: 🏛️ Exam 2026 general · reading: a father who teaches money values ⭐⭐

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2026, general — reading, question 1)
A text tells how David, a multimillionaire, raises his children.

The text is mainly about a father who

options.text: refused to pay for his kids' needs
taught his children money values
raised funds to help the homeless

questions.explanation: All three paragraphs show how David teaches his children to deal with money: that is teaching money values. He says he would gladly pay for his children's needs, so refusing them is wrong, and nobody in the text raises funds for anyone.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2026, general — reading, question 2a, paragraph 2)
The father of the family, a multimillionaire, explains how his children get money. Is the statement below true or false, going by paragraph 2?

"The kids get extra money whenever they want it."

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: The statement is false: a sentence of paragraph 2 says the opposite. Judge a statement by the words of the paragraph, not by what seems likely for the children of a rich father.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2026, general — reading, question 2a, paragraph 2)
A student says: "The kids get extra money whenever they want it." Which part of paragraph 2 settles whether this statement is true or false?

options.text: she asked if I would pay her to fix them
they didn't just get money if they asked
I was happy to hand over the money
one of my daughters once noted our doors were squeaking

questions.explanation: The father made his kids brainstorm and solve issues so they would learn that they did not just get money if they asked. This is the part that settles the statement. The daughter's request and the father's payment come with a job to do, so they do not show that money comes on demand.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2026, general — reading, question 2b, paragraph 3)
In paragraph 3, David talks about giving, saving and spending, and about one of his daughters. Decide whether the statement below is true or false.

"David's daughter follows her father's rules."

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: The statement is true: paragraph 3 gives an example that agrees with it. Judge a statement by the words of the paragraph, not by what seems likely.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2026, general — reading, question 2b, paragraph 3)
A student says: "David's daughter follows her father's rules." Which part of paragraph 3 settles whether this statement is true or false?

options.text: money should be used in three ways
I believe in talking about your financial values
daughter giving half of her $20 bill
society will fill the silence

questions.explanation: The father's rule is to use money for giving, saving and spending. His daughter giving half of her $20 bill to a homeless person is an example of the first use, so she follows his rule. The rule alone says nothing about the daughter, and the two other parts are about talking with children.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2026, general — reading, question 3, paragraph 1)
Paragraph 1 says: "David Ciccarelli, a multimillionaire, has made it clear that he won't be letting his kids live a lavish life." and "However, I refuse to spend funds on their wants, like a pair of trendy sneakers."

Which word from paragraph 1 means nearly the same as "luxurious"?

options.text: multimillionaire
trendy
lavish
gladly

questions.explanation: "Lavish" describes a life full of luxury and expensive things, so it is the word that means nearly the same as "luxurious". "Multimillionaire" names a rich person, not a kind of life, "trendy" means fashionable and "gladly" means willingly.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2026, general — reading, question 4, paragraph 2)
In paragraph 2 David says: "...one of my daughters once noted our doors were squeaking, so she asked if I would pay her to fix them."

What does "them" refer to?

options.text: his children
the doors
my daughters
the funds

questions.explanation: "Them" replaces the plural noun that the daughter offered to fix: the doors. Put it back in the sentence: she asked if he would pay her to fix the doors. The children and the daughters are people, and the funds are money: none of them is what the daughter fixes.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2026, general — reading, question 5)
The exam asks: "If you were one of David's kids, would you approve of his way of raising his children? Why or why not?" Think about a child who says YES.

Which reasons can this child give, according to the text?

options.text: Money must be earned, not just given.
The father pays for the children's wants as well as their needs.
The children learn three uses of money: giving, saving and spending.
The children get a salary without doing anything at home.
The father stops talking about money with his children.

questions.explanation: The text supports two reasons: David hates the idea of an allowance given rather than earned, and he teaches his children to give, save and spend. The other reasons go against the text: he refuses to pay for wants such as trendy sneakers, the salary depends on chores around the house, and he believes in talking about financial values with kids.
